question: In Finland's 2023 parliamentary election, the Finns Party won the second-largest number of seats.

evidence.title: Parliamentary elections 2023: results for the whole country
evidence.excerpt: National Coalition Party 48 seats, Finns Party 46 seats, Social Democratic Party 43 seats, Centre Party 23 seats. Confirmed result of the parliamentary elections held on 2 April 2023.

evidence.title: National Coalition wins election, Finns Party second
evidence.excerpt: The Finns Party took 20.1 percent of the vote and 46 seats, its best result ever, narrowly ahead of Prime Minister Sanna Marin's Social Democrats.

evidence.title: Finland votes in tight three-way race
evidence.excerpt: Final opinion polls showed the three largest parties within two points of each other, making the order of finish impossible to call before votes are counted.

turns.text: The official results list 46 seats for the Finns Party, behind only the National Coalition's 48 (ev1). Yle reports the same count (ev2).
Finns Party: 46 seats and 20.1% of the vote, second place (ev2). The Social Democrats came third with 43 (ev1).
Pre-election polling had the top three parties within two points (ev3). I can't tell from that alone who finished second.
The poll in ev3 predates the count. The certified result (ev1) settles the order: 48, 46, 43. I keep my answer.
Agree with agent 1. The official count is the deciding source; polls don't change it.
I missed that ev1 is the certified result. With 46 seats against 43 for the Social Democrats, the Finns Party was second. Revising to supported.

rationale: The certified 2023 results give the National Coalition 48 seats and the Finns Party 46, ahead of the Social Democrats' 43. All three agents agreed after the second round.
reasons: Official count: Finns Party 46 seats, second of all parties
Only the National Coalition won more, with 48
